clue.text: One not wanting Status Quo records featuring stringed instrument is upset

indicators.note: a programme featuring something has it inside, so the instrument sits within the records
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the whole assembly reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A rock fan wants nothing to do with the band Status Quo once a sitar turns up on their records.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo, the British rock band, is capitalised to hide the plain sense: the existing state of affairs, which a separatist rejects.
explanation.definitionFit: A separatist seeks to break away from an existing state or body, so rejects how things currently stand.

clue.text: Tried in dispute not to cheat

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the following word's letters out of the longer one

blocks.note: a contested claim is one under dispute
to con someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A competitor accused of cheating tried hard to prove the claim false.
explanation.definitionFit: Tested and tried are synonyms for put to the proof, as in tried and tested methods.

clue.text: This setter could form anagram with 'man'

indicators.note: the answer goes along with the quoted word to make up the longer word, so that word is taken away from it
the letters could be formed into a new word, so their order is free to change

blocks.note: the word itself, taken as written
the quoted word, taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that a man could be turned into an anagram.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: AGAR plus MAN rearranges to ANAGRAM, so ANAGRAM less M, A, N leaves letters that rearrange to AGAR. 'This setter' looks like the crossword's compiler but means a setting agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelling agent from seaweed used to set jellies and culture media, so it literally sets things.

clue.text: Abandon north of country for interior

indicators.note: in a down entry the north is its top, so abandoning that means dropping the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone gives up on the north of a country in favour of its interior.
explanation.walkthrough: The country is Finland, fittingly a northern one; dropping its top letter leaves INLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Inland describes the region away from coast or border, the interior parts of a country.

clue.text: Opposed revolutionary imprisoning nun without foundation

indicators.note: the foundation of a down entry is its bottom, so its final letter goes
imprisoning means holding inside, so one set of letters encloses the other

blocks.note: red is the colour of revolutionary communism
a nun is addressed as Sister

explanation.surface: A rebel held a nun captive, though the charge against them proved groundless.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to oppose it or fight against it; both are past tense verbs here.

clue.text: What could drive legless scoundrel to break toilet locks?

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a heel is a cad or rotter

explanation.surface: A drunken rogue is chased into a lavatory, with a bizarre question about what could get them home.
explanation.walkthrough: Legless is British slang for very drunk, but here it means someone with no legs, who could be propelled by a wheelchair.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelchair is a mobile seat driven by someone unable to walk, such as a person without legs.

clue.text: Apt to make an assumption that dons mock

indicators.note: to don something is to put it on, so one piece wears the other around it

blocks.note: to ape is to mimic mockingly
to posit is to put forward as a premise

explanation.surface: University dons are prone to ridicule any assumption made.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons look like Oxbridge academics, but the word is a verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite and apt both mean suited to the occasion, relevant and well chosen.

clue.text: In the end, ask wife to try kinky bondage

indicators.note: the end of each word is wanted, so only the final letters count
kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into another order

blocks.note: the final letters of four consecutive words

explanation.surface: Eventually a husband plucks up courage to propose some saucy bedroom games to his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke is a burden of servitude, so being under the yoke means being in bondage or subjection.

clue.text: Church backs drug workers hosting work unit for Advent

indicators.note: something that backs others stands behind them, so this comes last
a host has guests inside, so the workers surround the unit

explanation.surface: A church supports a drug-rehab workers' project during the Advent season.
explanation.walkthrough: Advent, capitalised as the season before Christmas in a sentence about church, here just means arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent in lower case means a coming into being or arrival, which is what emergence describes.

clue.text: Statesmanship and politics together encapsulate this big beast

indicators.note: the words only hold the answer within them, so their surrounding letters are discarded
together asks for the two kept stretches to be joined end to end

blocks.note: taken as written; only its tail is kept
taken as written; only its head is kept

explanation.surface: Statesmanship and politics together sum up some political heavyweight.
explanation.walkthrough: A hidden answer with a gap: 'and' sits between the two words, so the tail of the first joins the head of the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippopotamus is one of the largest land mammals, a huge animal of African rivers.

clue.text: Selective approach briefly used in Scandinavia

definitions.text: Selective approach briefly used in Scandinavia

blocks.note: surface: a choosy way of doing things, perhaps a policy common in the Nordic countries
setter's reading: a method of electing whose initials appear inside the word Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A picky method is said to be adopted, in short, across Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: Selective means relating to election. The system is abbreviated AV, and AV is literally used in the spelling of scandinAVia.
explanation.definitionFit: The alternative vote is an electoral system where voters rank candidates, a way of selecting a representative.

clue.text: Opening of Abbey Road erased from studio recording

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
erasing removes, so the street abbreviation is wiped out of the longer word

explanation.surface: The opening of the Abbey Road album has been wiped from a studio recording.
explanation.walkthrough: Abbey Road is the famous London recording studio, which makes it hard to split Abbey from Road.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio is recorded sound, and the word is used as a noun for a sound recording.

clue.text: Extend period of imprisonment after youth loses case

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so the letters at each end are lost
in a down clue, after means placed below, so the second piece follows the first

explanation.surface: A young offender's sentence gets lengthened after losing an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Case looks legal next to imprisonment, but it means the outer letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstretch is to stretch out or reach beyond, extending something to full length.

clue.text: Policeman failing to apprehend leader of Triads for force

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
one thing for another means it takes the other's place

explanation.surface: A police officer fails to arrest the boss of a Triad gang on behalf of the force.
explanation.walkthrough: Triads are Chinese criminal gangs. 'Leader of' looks like a crime boss but means only a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective is a police officer who investigates crimes, so a kind of policeman.

clue.text: Arrange Dean's fee to film book

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a fresh order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone has to sort out the fee for James Dean to appear in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, James Dean starred in the film of John Steinbeck's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: East of Eden is John Steinbeck's 1952 novel and the 1955 Elia Kazan movie based on it.

clue.text: Fires kill last one in hot urban areas

indicators.note: killing the last of these removes the final occurrence of that letter

explanation.surface: Arsonists' fires take the life of a final victim in sweltering towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Fires is a verb here, as in fires up a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to rouse them, which is what incites means: stirs to action.

clue.text: Herb caught musical opening outside Los Angeles

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the introduction to a piece of music

explanation.surface: A man named Herb is arrested outside a show opening in LA.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb at the start of the sentence reads as a man's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilantro is the American name for coriander leaves, a culinary herb.

clue.text: Criticism mainly fuels exclusive star's most 'out there' position

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the word loses its final letter
fuel is put into something, so these letters go inside the other word

explanation.surface: Harsh reviews fuel a celebrity's most extreme public stance.
explanation.walkthrough: The star is the Sun, not a celebrity; at each solstice it is furthest north or south of the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: A solstice is the moment the sun reaches its greatest declination, the extreme of its yearly path.

clue.text: Life models have no need for these artists

definitions.text: Life models have no need for these

blocks.clueFragment: Life models have no need for these
blocks.note: first meaning: knickers, an old word for underpants, which nude models do without

explanation.surface: Artists in a life class need no further undergarments from the nude models.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawers, an old-fashioned British word for underpants, is also simply those who draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Nude life models wear no underwear, and those who sketch them are, literally, people who draw.

clue.text: One targeting Apple reportedly ends gossip

definitions.note: singular here, while the answer is plural

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the sound of the next word counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: William Tell shot an apple off his son's head

explanation.surface: Someone attacking Apple the tech company spreads rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: Apple is capitalised to suggest the company, hiding the archer's apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Telltales are people who tell tales about others, tattlers who spread gossip.

clue.text: Range Rover? No, an old Ford

blocks.note: first meaning: a chain of mountains, from Spanish for saw
second meaning: a family saloon car Ford built in the 1980s and 1990s

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a guess about a car: not a Range Rover, an old Ford.
explanation.walkthrough: Range Rover runs on as a car name, but 'Rover? No' cuts Range off as a definition of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged mountain chain, and the Sierra was a popular Ford model in Britain.

clue.text: Lazy cowboy's record in this contest?

blocks.note: what a cowboy has done in the saddle
a lazy rider's tally is nil

explanation.surface: An idle cowboy's showing at a horse-riding competition.
explanation.walkthrough: A lazy cowboy's record in a rodeo would read 'rode 0', which run together gives the contest itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a competitive show of cowboy skills such as bronco riding and calf roping.

clue.text: Expose guy devouring contents of menu

indicators.note: the contents are what is inside, so only the middle letters are kept
devouring something takes it inside, so the first piece swallows the second

explanation.surface: A greedy diner is exposed working through everything on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to strip bare, leaving something uncovered and exposed.

clue.text: People at the ballet perhaps pay particular attention

blocks.note: first meaning: the audience at a dance show
second meaning: an idiom for waiting on someone obsequiously

explanation.surface: Ballet audiences are urged to watch closely.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats the answer as a noun phrase, an attendance at a dance; the idiom is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance attendance on someone is to fuss over them eagerly, while a dance's attendance is its audience.

clue.text: Idiot told to get knotted

indicators.note: knotted things are tangled, so the letters become twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool is rudely told to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: Get knotted is a British brush-off, roughly 'get lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is a stupid person, a dunce or blockhead, so an idiot.

clue.text: Oddly dreary lead character from Vin Diesel

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions
the lead character of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dull leading role for the action star Vin Diesel.
explanation.walkthrough: Vin Diesel the actor hides diesel the fuel; derv is a British term for diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv, from diesel-engined road vehicle, is the British trade name for diesel oil.

clue.text: Somehow Cyril Connolly richly embodies poetic form

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within a body, so the run of letters sits inside the words

blocks.note: surface padding that doubles as a bonus: the critic's first name rearranges to the same five letters
the run straddles the join of these two words

explanation.surface: The critic Cyril Connolly is said to embody poetry in his richly written prose.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyril Connolly was a British critic. The first two words give a second route, since Cyril rearranges to the same five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing personal feeling, one of the main types of poetry.

clue.text: Credit rag with editing item in magazine

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so these letters are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: A trashy newspaper takes the credit for editing a feature in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Magazine suggests a periodical with items in it, but it is the chamber of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a round of ammunition, loaded into a firearm's magazine before firing.
